subject: Clarify data-use guarantee & deletion scenarios — playbook request
messages:
From: Lena Park <privacy@finovate.com>

Subject: Quick Qs on 'we do not train on customer data' — edge scenarios

Hi Hannah / Marissa,

Thanks for the earlier call. Before our procurement review I need a short written FAQ we can share internally. Our legal and engineering teams have three edge scenarios they want explicit confirmation on:

1) Debug snapshots & ephemeral logs (stack traces that include customer request payloads) — are these ever used to train models or surfaced into training datasets? What is the retention/TTL for these?
2) Backups / cold archives (S3 Glacier / offline snapshots) — if a customer requests deletion will those backups be purged, or do they remain until retention expiry?
3) Replication across regions & vendor-managed backups — could copies end up in training corpora due to partner processes?

Also: what is your tombstone / permanent deletion timeline after a customer requests erase? And are there any exceptions (legal hold, billing disputes, security investigations)?

If you can attach a short playbook or bulleted policy we can attach to the RFP that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Lena

Subject: Re: Quick Qs on 'we do not train on customer data' — edge scenarios

Hi Lena —

Appreciate the clear list. High-level answer up front: Redwood does not incorporate customer-provided production data into model training datasets. Below I summarize operational policies and include a short draft playbook attached (redwood-delete-playbook-draft.pdf) that we recommend you share with procurement/legal.

Summary bullets:
- Training: No production customer data is used to train our models. We maintain a separation between customer inference traffic and any training pipelines.
- Telemetry & debug snapshots: Short-lived telemetry (performance metrics and traces) is retained for troubleshooting (default 30 days), debug snapshots that include full payloads are rotated out within 90 days unless explicitly preserved for a security investigation.
- Backups / archives: Backups are stored according to configurable retention tiers. Cold archives (>=365 days) are retained for disaster recovery; deletions are processed via a tombstone flow — once a delete request is issued we mark records for purge and exclude them from active systems, and we schedule removal from backups at the next archive retention cycle unless a legal hold is present.
- Regional replication: Copies are replicated for availability only. No replication process writes to training pipelines. Third-party vendor processes that access backups are governed by vendor contracts and SCAs; we can provide summary evidence.
- Exceptions: Legal holds, active security forensics, or billing disputes can delay permanent purge. We surface exceptions in our erase confirmation and provide a case-level owner.

Action items:
1) Ben — can you add specifics about snapshot types and exact retention TTLs in the playbook?
2) Marissa — I attached the draft playbook (redwood-delete-playbook-draft.pdf) for Finovate review; can you review the wording on vendor backups and provide a short attestation text we can include?

Will respond with a slightly expanded playbook and a suggested attestation clause by EOD tomorrow. Let me know if you want an explicit attestation letter or a contract addendum.

Best,
Hannah

Hannah — adding technical specifics to the thread below so Finovate sees concrete numbers.

- Debug snapshots: two classes — (A) ephemeral traces (metrics, spans, redacted headers) retained 30 days; (B) full debug dumps (payloads + stack) retained 90 days. Full dumps are accessible to SRE/infra on a need-to-debug basis and are not exported to any ML training storage.
- KV/prefix caches: ephemeral caches are in-memory or GPU-backed and evicted within 24–72 hours depending on workload; we do not snapshot these caches into training stores.
- Backups: daily logical backups kept for 30 days in hot tier, 90 days in warm tier, and up to 365 days in cold (configurable). When a delete is requested we tombstone the customer identifier and exclude it from active queries immediately. Purge from cold archives happens on the next scheduled retention compaction (within 90 days of the delete request by default).
- Vendor-managed copies: we require subprocessors to sign SCAs that prohibit using customer data for modeling. We include subcontractor lists in SOC2 evidence.
- Permanent deletion: our workflow marks data as deleted (tombstoned) immediately, then runs asynchronous purge jobs; final irrecoverable deletion for archive-tier copies is typically completed within 90 days unless a legal hold is applied.

If Finovate wants a tighter SLA (e.g., purge from all tiers within 30 days) we can propose a dedicated process as part of a Dedicated/Private offering and document it in the Statement of Work.

—Ben

Subject: Final: Written Q&A + next steps on attestation and contract language

Lena / Finovate legal ops —

Thanks for the questions and for giving us a chance to clarify. Attached is the playbook (redwood-delete-playbook-draft.pdf) plus a short evidence workbook (evidence-summary-2027.xlsx) that maps the statements above to SOC2 controls and subprocessor attestations. Key confirmations:

• Non-training guarantee: Redwood does not use customer production data to train or fine-tune models. This is an engineering and process boundary — training pipelines are logically and operationally separate from inference logs and backups.
• Immediate exclusion: Upon an erase request we exclude the customer from active systems immediately (tombstone) so no further inference traffic is associated with the identity.
• Archive purge timeline: Cold archive purge completes within 90 days of request by default; we can negotiate shorter windows under a contract for Dedicated/Private customers.
• Exceptions: Legal hold, security incident investigations, and regulatory obligations may delay irreversible deletion; we will notify you and provide a case owner and expected timeline.

Next steps we propose:
1) Katie on Finovate legal — if you’re comfortable with the wording we can prepare either: (A) an attestation letter for procurement; or (B) a contract addendum with a tailored TTL and a DocuSign envelope (link included).
2) We will provide a short vendor/subprocessor list and SOC2 extract for your procurement pack.

If you want, Marissa can join a 30-minute call to walk through the playbook and evidence workbook and capture any edits in real time.

Best regards,
Hannah
